glosses: to dial in, to dial up (to connect to a system or service by telephone)
sich durch einen technischen Vorgang (früher nur über das Wählen einer Telefonnummer) in einem Informationssystem anmelden, den Kontakt/die Verbindung dazu herstellen

examples.text: Windows versucht, sich automatisch in das Internet einzuwählen, wenn man die Hilfefunktion aufruft.

translations.source_sense_description: sich durch einen technischen Vorgang in einem Informationssystem anmelden

glosses: To telephone, to call on the telephone.
To connect a computer to a modem.
To increase the level (of something) by turning a dial, or (figuratively) as if by turning a dial.

examples.text: These comments are guaranteed to dial up the animosity.
Think Bernie Sanders versus Kamala Harris, but dialled up to France where revolution is part of the national psyche.

translations.source_sense_description: sich durch einen technischen Vorgang in einem Informationssystem anmelden

glosses: To configure or set up (particularly a complex machine with many configuration options [especially knobs and dials]).

examples.text: Before starting the recording, make sure you've dialled in the right synthesiser settings.

glosses: To connect (to a system or service) by telephone.

examples.text: I tried dialling in to the server, but I couldn't connect.

glosses: To join or participate in (a conference call).

examples.text: Did you dial in to that earnings announcement?

glosses: To apprehend and align oneself (to an idea, circumstance, way of thinking, etc.).

examples.text: The company quickly dialled in to the fact that customers wanted greater convenience.
Nowadays most people are dialled in to the idea that smoking is bad for you.

Starting in the ’90s, politicians began treating elections like advertising campaigns and used focus groups to dial in the most effective rhetoric, according to the Stanford economist Matthew Gentzkow, who has analyzed congressional speeches.
